plan: My private value is $10. In a single-round game with rational bidders, the optimal strategy is to bid strategically near my value. Since the second-highest bid determines the payment, I want to bid just enough to potentially win without overpaying. Given the $0-$49 range, I'll bid slightly above my value at $10.5 to signal serious intent while minimizing potential loss if I don't win.

My private value is $30. In a single-round auction with rational bidders, the optimal strategy is to bid slightly below my true value. Since the prize is worth $30 to me, I want to win if possible, but minimize my payment. I'll bid $29.9 - this is close to my true value but leaves room to potentially profit if I win. Other rational bidders will likely use similar strategies around their private values.

My private value is $25. In a second-price sealed bid auction, the optimal strategy is to bid my true value. By bidding $25, I maximize my potential profit:
- If I win, I'll pay less than my bid
- If my bid is higher than others, I capture the surplus
- Bidding above true value risks overpaying
- Bidding below true value risks losing when I could have won profitably
